account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: morning office business, the mill grain inspection, lunch at home, council correspondence, and tea with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage. I returned to the office at 16:50, late for my 16:30 appointment, and have just asked the secretary what needs attention. The great-hall lighting and table inspection with the builder is scheduled for 18:00, before I go home at 19:00.

The unusual news is a repeated but unconfirmed rumour about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk have associated the baker, innkeeper, neighbour, Freight, and builder with being there. I have heard no clear description of an actual change or its purpose. I crossed the bridge without trouble. At tea, my neighbour explicitly said they had neither witnessed a change nor learned anything definite, and did not want to repeat the rumour as fact. They said the dock was peaceful and that the baker had reported a well-stocked market. Reports of the baker carrying a sack of bread do not by themselves establish anything unusual.

At the mill stall I saw seventy-seven hay bales available. Council letters, however, have not been found: the secretary checked the office chest and identified only my schedule copy and updated appointment book. I asked for the correspondence to be located before my return; I am awaiting an update. Earlier the secretary could not find Freight or the builder at their workplaces and had no confirmed report on hall preparations. My latest question was heard by both the secretary and builder, though I cannot currently see the builder. The neighbour has also now appeared near the office; I do not know why.

My best grounded explanation for the known preparations is ordinary town business: the scheduled hall inspection concerns lighting and tables. I do not know whether it has any connection to the bakery rumours, and have no evidence establishing a hidden purpose or an actual crossing change.
